topic: Using std::set insert() Method and Return Value
explanation: In C++, the standard library container std::set provides a member function insert() that attempts to insert a new element into the set. Unlike some containers, insert() returns a std::pair consisting of an iterator to the element and a boolean indicating whether the insertion took place. This allows programmers to determine if the insertion was successful (i.e., the element was not already present) and to access the position of the inserted or existing element. This feature is essential for efficient set operations, especially when duplicate elements are not allowed, and understanding the return value helps manage element insertion logic effectively.
